about.title: A path of adaptation, learning and execution.
paragraphs: I am a Cuban software developer based in Curitiba, Brazil, under refugee status. My path combines logistics management, self-taught learning and constant software engineering practice.

Today I build full-stack products and self-hosted systems: an omnichannel AI CRM, web/Android operations platforms, live chat, a native download manager for Ubuntu, desktop tools and utilities for AI agents.

I focus on solving real problems with TypeScript, Node.js, Python, Rust, React/Next.js, Kotlin, GTK4/Libadwaita, PostgreSQL/Supabase, Docker and Linux, while caring about experience, security and maintainability.
I believe technology is my best language for creating value: clear documentation, automated tests and reproducible deployments are part of the product.
timeline: Spot repetitive processes and turn them into systems.
Design simple, maintainable tools that are useful from day one.
Iterate with real data, clear documentation and a product mindset.

projects.name: CRM Sofia Manager
projects.subtitle: Omnichannel AI CRM for orders and support
projects.description: Web platform to manage orders, omnichannel support and stock for a Sunday roast operation, with Sofia AI across WhatsApp, Telegram and web, a real-time operator console and Pix/Mercado Pago payments.
projects.does: Unifies conversations, cart, orders, inventory, payments and reports; Sofia answers with RAG over the menu and hands off to humans when needed.
projects.problem: The Sunday operation relied on scattered messages and manual stock control, making overselling, lost orders and late payment reconciliation easy.

sections.title: Problem
sections.text: Orders across WhatsApp, Telegram and web without a single source of truth; finite stock, pickup slots and payments that required manual reconciliation.

sections.title: Implemented solution
sections.text: Next.js 16, TypeScript and Supabase/PostgreSQL 17 with RLS and atomic RPCs; DeepSeek RAG, Evolution API and Telegram, a Realtime console and idempotent Mercado Pago/Pix webhooks, all in Docker.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.text: One source of truth for the operation, transactional stock, real-time support and reconciled payments; v0.1.0 with 2,827 test cases and green CI.

methods: Docker Compose (recommended): clone, configure the environment and start the services.
Local development: Node.js 22, npm and a Supabase instance.
steps: Clone the repository and copy .env.example to .env.
Configure Supabase, DeepSeek, Evolution and Mercado Pago.
Run docker compose up -d --build and open port 3000.
caseStudy.command: git clone https://github.com/wilkin-barban/CRM_Sofia_Manager.git && cd CRM_Sofia_Manager && docker compose up -d --build

projects.name: Segmenta
projects.subtitle: Native download manager for Ubuntu
projects.description: Segmented HTTP/HTTPS download manager with torrents, YouTube and public HLS/DASH for Ubuntu 26.04, with its own daemon, CLI, GTK4/Libadwaita GUI and browser extension.
projects.does: Splits downloads across up to 32 connections, resumes after closing the GUI or rebooting, captures browser downloads with confirmation and unifies HTTP, torrents and media in one queue.
projects.problem: Browsers lose long downloads when the tab closes, the session sleeps or the machine reboots; there is no single place to manage direct downloads, torrents and media.

sections.title: Problem
sections.text: Long downloads depended on an open tab, and there was no single queue for HTTP, torrents and media.

sections.title: Implemented solution
sections.text: Rust daemon with SQLite WAL and JSON-RPC over a Unix socket, segmented engine with hot-split and resume, GTK4/Libadwaita GUI, CLI, Chromium/Firefox extension and embedded yt-dlp.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.text: Downloads survive the GUI and reboot, with real progress, queues, browser capture and an installable Ubuntu 26.04 .deb; v0.5.0 with green CI.

methods: Download the .deb from the release and enable segmenta.socket.
Build from the repository with Rust and package with cargo-deb.
steps: Download segmenta_0.5.0-1_amd64.deb and verify its SHA-256.
Install with apt and run systemctl --user enable --now segmenta.socket.
Open Segmenta from the app menu or run segmenta-gui.
caseStudy.command: git clone https://github.com/wilkin-barban/Segmenta.git && cd Segmenta && packaging/fetch-ytdlp.sh && cargo build --release --workspace

projects.name: Trindade Massas
projects.subtitle: Plant operations on web and Android
projects.description: Platform for dough production, hygiene and temperature reports, loading schedule, stock and administration; responsive web, native Android and Aero32 ERP integration.
projects.does: Records production by product and box, photo reports, loading slots, stock and calculators; keeps the same business rules on web and Android.
projects.problem: The plant used spreadsheets and messages; traceability, slot control and web/Android parity were missing.

sections.title: Problem
sections.text: Scattered production and controls, error risk and little visibility into the plant's state.

sections.title: Implemented solution
sections.text: Monorepo with a Fastify/SQLite API, React/Vite SPA, Kotlin/Compose Android app, OpenAPI contracts, Docker/Nginx and Aero32 integration; CI and signed Android releases.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.text: Web and mobile operations with shared rules, auditable records, reliable stock and slots, and reproducible deployment; v0.8.6.

methods: Web: sign in to the deployed instance with your plant user.
Development: Node.js 24, npm, Docker and make.
steps: Clone the repo and run make install.
Copy .env.example to .env and set JWT_SECRET.
Run make dev and open http://localhost:5173.
caseStudy.command: git clone https://github.com/wilkin-barban/Trindade.git && cd Trindade && make install && make dev

projects.name: Super Chat Manager
projects.subtitle: Self-hosted live chat with AI and Telegram
projects.description: Self-hosted chat manager with an embeddable widget, admin panel, Telegram integration, RAG knowledge base, SQLite and Docker; successor to LiveChat Pro.
projects.does: Adds chat to any site with one script, keeps sessions and history, sends messages to Telegram and the panel, supports replies from both and uses admin-approved RAG.
projects.problem: SaaS chat adds cost and dependency; data control, Telegram and a private knowledge base were missing.

sections.title: Problem
sections.text: External chat without data control, direct Telegram integration or a private knowledge base.

sections.title: Implemented solution
sections.text: Node.js 24, Socket.IO, SQLite, Redis and Docker; widget and public configuration; responsive admin; approved-index RAG; Telegram bot; CI and GHCR images.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.text: Self-hosted chat with persistent history, Telegram or panel operations, controlled RAG and reproducible deployment; v1.2.0.

methods: One-click installer on Linux (Docker) or Windows (Node.js).
Manual Docker Compose for a VPS with domain and reverse proxy.
steps: Run the installer and follow the wizard.
Configure Telegram, credentials and allowed origin.
Start the service and paste the widget into the site.

projects.name: FF-Converter
projects.subtitle: Desktop batch FFmpeg converter
projects.description: Electron app for Windows and Linux that batch-converts video and audio with bundled FFmpeg, reusable profiles, queue, watched folders, GPU diagnostics and logs.
projects.does: Drag files or folders, choose a profile and destination, process in a queue, resume jobs, switch language/theme and check for updates.
projects.problem: Batch conversion with FFmpeg required commands, paths and versions; there was no stable UI for profiles, queues and diagnostics.

sections.title: Problem
sections.text: Manual conversion workflows, risk of incorrect commands and little progress visibility.

sections.title: Implemented solution
sections.text: Electron and TypeScript, bundled FFmpeg with manifest and hashes, persistent queue, profiles, GPU diagnostics, i18n, electron-builder and signed releases.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.text: Cross-platform local batch conversion with logs, recovery and updates; v1.1.1.

methods: Windows: .exe installer from the latest release.
Linux: AppImage or .deb package; FFmpeg and FFprobe are included.
steps: Download the package for your system from the release.
Open the app and drag files or a folder.
Choose a profile and destination, then add to the queue.
caseStudy.command: git clone https://github.com/wilkin-barban/FF-Converter.git && cd FF-Converter && npm ci && npm run dev

projects.name: pi-auto-compaction
projects.subtitle: Automatic compaction for Pi agents
projects.description: Extension for Pi, gentle-shell and herdr that decouples compaction from the conversation model, with configurable summarizers, multi-tier fallback, local telemetry and doctor.
projects.does: Summarizes history with dedicated models, lets you choose primary and fallback, applies per-model policies, protects quota and offers read-only diagnostics.
projects.problem: Native compaction consumes the expensive model and can trigger too early; without fallback, a long session breaks.

sections.title: Problem
sections.text: Compaction coupled to the main model, opaque thresholds and a single point of failure.

sections.title: Implemented solution
sections.text: TypeScript extension without monkey-patching, isolated settings, 60s/120s fallback, policies for 8 models, allowlisted telemetry, immutable deploy and Node 22/24 CI.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.text: Longer, cheaper and more stable sessions with explicit control and diagnostics; 326 tests across 33 suites and v1.2.1.

methods: Manual install from the repo with Node.js 22.19+.
Download the source archive from the latest release.
steps: Clone the repo and install dependencies.
Run npm run deploy -- --dry-run and review the report.
Run npm run deploy and reload the Pi session.
caseStudy.command: git clone https://github.com/wilkin-barban/pi-auto-compaction.git && cd pi-auto-compaction && npm ci --ignore-scripts && npm run deploy -- --dry-run

projects.name: Cauce
projects.subtitle: Native batch multimedia converter for Ubuntu
projects.description: Native batch multimedia converter and orchestrator for Ubuntu 26.04 powered by a persistent Rust daemon, modern GTK4/Libadwaita GUI, SQLite WAL, and 13 tuned system presets using system FFmpeg.
projects.does: Manages video and audio conversions in the background surviving GUI closure, inspects media via ffprobe, provides 13 immutable presets for Smart TVs, web, and audio, and monitors real-time telemetry.
projects.problem: Traditional conversion tools rely on open windows or heavy web wrappers (Electron) that consume excessive memory and abort conversions if the desktop session closes.

sections.title: Problem
sections.text: Batch media conversion on Linux required complex terminal pipelines or bloated Electron interfaces that cannot keep queues alive when the UI closes.

sections.title: Implemented solution
sections.text: Client-daemon architecture in Rust with SQLite WAL persistence, JSON-RPC IPC over Unix sockets, system FFmpeg/FFprobe orchestration, and native GTK4 + Libadwaita desktop client.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.text: Concurrent conversions with live telemetry (FPS, speed, ETA), 13 calibrated presets, seamless GNOME desktop integration, and a clean .deb package for Ubuntu 26.04.

methods: Download the .deb package from GitHub Releases and enable cauce.socket.
Build from source using Rust and Cargo.
steps: Download cauce_0.1.1-1_amd64.deb from the latest release.
Install with sudo dpkg -i cauce_0.1.1-1_amd64.deb and enable systemctl --user enable --now cauce.socket.
Launch Cauce from the application menu or run cauce-gui.
caseStudy.command: git clone https://github.com/wilkin-barban/Cauce.git && cd Cauce && cargo build --release
